title: Eliot Bochet-Merand
text:
Automation shifts which tasks machines perform. Immigration shifts who performs the rest. They arrive together, and the labour market resolves them jointly — yet we study them apart.
I am a PhD candidate at Paris Nanterre University, in the EconomiX research centre, supervised by Lionel Ragot. My thesis asks how technical change, human capital and immigration interact in the labour market, using French administrative data accessed through the CASD.
I came to economics through its philosophy: before this thesis I worked on Samuelson’s expected utility concept at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne, and spent a year producing an economics programme for France Culture. Both still shape how I choose questions and how I try to explain answers.

title: Reproducibility with restricted-access data
text: Parts of this research use data accessed through the Centre d’acces securise aux donnees (CASD). No observation can leave the enclave. Confidentiality restricts the data, not the code : everything except the microdata is published here.

title: Reproducibility with restricted-access data
text:
What is available
The full pipeline. Cleaning, variable construction, and every specification, in the order they run.
A synthetic data generator. It reproduces the structure of the source files (the same variables, types, and plausible marginal distributions) with no real observation. Clone the repository, run the pipeline on synthetic input, and the whole chain executes. A referee can audit the logic without clearance.
A metadata dictionary. Every variable, its source file, and how it was built.

title: Reproducibility with restricted-access data
text:
What is not, and why
The microdata. Access runs through a CASD application.

title: Reproducibility with restricted-access data
text:
Why bother
Journals now require a data availability statement, and work on confidential data usually answers with a paragraph of apology. A synthetic generator plus a public pipeline is a better answer: it makes the claim checkable rather than merely stated.
